s: canon new f-1：機械與電子之間的專業旗艦  canon new f-1: a professional flagship between mechanics and electronics      在 canon 的單鏡反光機歷史上，new f-1 是一部承先啟後的機型。它是手動對焦 fd 系統的最後一部專業旗艦，亦是 canon 在機械相機和電子相機之間取得最佳平衡的作品。它在1981年面世，陪伴無數新聞和體育攝影師走過整個八十年代。 一、f-1 的傳承 1971年，canon 推出第一代 f-1，正式向 nikon f 系列在專業市場的地位發起挑戰。f-1 以堅固耐用和系統完整見稱，其後在1976年推出改良版 f-1n。 到了八十年代初，電子化已成為大勢所趨，自動曝光逐漸普及。canon 需要一部既保留專業機械可靠性，又能提供現代電子功能的新旗艦，new f-1 就在這個背景下誕生。 二、混合式快門：電池耗盡也能拍 new f-1 最受稱道的設計，是它的混合式快門。高速檔由機械控制，即使電池耗盡，仍然可以用這些速度繼續拍攝；慢速檔和自動曝光則由電子控制，提供更高的精度。 對專業攝影師來說，這個設計非常實際。在嚴寒的戶外、偏遠的地區或者長時間的採訪中，電池隨時可能失效，有了機械快門作後備，相機就不會因此「罷工」。快門簾採用鈦金屬薄片製造，耐用度和精度都達到專業要求。 三、模組化的系統設計 new f-1 的核心理念是「模組化」，攝影師可以按需要更換不同組件，把相機配置成最適合自己的工具。 可換觀景器：標準眼平觀景器提供手動曝光；換上 ae 觀景器後，相機便可進行光圈優先自動曝光。此外還有腰平觀景器和高倍率觀景器等選擇，適合微距、翻拍和特殊用途。 馬達與自動曝光：裝上 ae 電動捲片器或 ae 馬達後，相機便可以進行快門優先自動曝光，同時提供連續拍攝功能。換句話說，同一部 new f-1，可以按配件組合變成手動、光圈優先或快門優先相機。 可換對焦屏：new f-1 有多款對焦屏可供選擇。更特別的是，更換對焦屏亦會改變測光方式，攝影師可以按題材選擇平均測光、局部測光或點測光。這種把測光模式和對焦屏結合的設計，在同期相機中十分獨特。 四、為專業而生的耐用性 new f-1 的機身由金屬製造，結構堅固，能承受新聞、體育和野外攝影的嚴苛環境。canon 在設計時特別重視可靠性，機身經過嚴格測試，在極端溫度和長時間使用下仍能穩定運作。 這部相機很快成為專業攝影師的主力器材，在新聞現場和大型體育賽事中經常可以見到它的身影。canon 亦推出了洛杉磯奧運紀念版，突顯它在體育攝影界的地位。 五、fd 鏡頭系統 new f-1 採用 canon fd 卡口，可以使用龐大的 fd 鏡頭群，由超廣角、標準以至超長焦鏡頭一應俱全。當中的 l 系列鏡頭採用螢石和特殊低色散鏡片，畫質出色，是新聞和體育攝影師的重要工具。完整的鏡頭和配件系統，令 new f-1 能夠應付幾乎所有拍攝需要。 六、fd 時代的終章 1987年，canon 推出 eos 自動對焦系統，改用全新的 ef 卡口，fd 系統逐步被取代。new f-1 一直生產至九十年代初，成為 fd 系統最後一部專業旗艦。canon 其後的專業旗艦，例如 eos-1，已全面進入自動對焦年代。 今天，new f-1 在二手市場仍然受到不少菲林愛好者和收藏家追捧。它堅固的機身、靈活的配置，以及機械快門帶來的安心感，令它在菲林攝影復興的年代再次發光。 七、結語 new f-1 是一部在時代交界處誕生的相機。它擁抱電子化帶來的便利，卻沒有放棄機械相機的可靠；它以模組化設計回應不同攝影師的需要，展現了 canon 對專業市場的深刻理解。作為 fd 系統的最後旗艦，new f-1 不只是一部相機，更是 canon 手動對焦時代的總結。  the new f-1 holds a pivotal place in the history of canon slrs. it was the last professional flagship of the manual-focus fd system, and the camera in which canon struck its best balance between mechanical and electronic design. it appeared in 1981 and went on to serve countless news and sports photographers throughout the 1980s. the f-1 heritage in 1971 canon launched the original f-1, its direct challenge to the nikon f series in the professional market. the f-1 was known for its toughness and complete system, and an improved version, the f-1n, followed in 1976. by the early 1980s, electronics were clearly the way forward and automatic exposure was becoming common. canon needed a new flagship that kept the mechanical reliability professionals depended on while offering modern electronic features. the new f-1 was born from that need. a hybrid shutter: keep shooting when the battery dies the new f-1's most admired feature is its hybrid shutter. the fast speeds are mechanically controlled, so you can keep shooting at those speeds even with a dead battery. the slow speeds and automatic exposure are electronically controlled for greater precision. for professional photographers this was a very practical design. in freezing conditions outdoors, in remote locations or on long assignments, a battery can fail at any moment. with a mechanical shutter as a back-up, the camera doesn't simply stop working. the shutter curtains are made of thin titanium foil, which gives them professional-grade durability and precision. a modular system the core idea behind the new f-1 is modularity. photographers could swap components to configure the camera into exactly the tool they needed. interchangeable finders: the standard eye-level finder gives manual exposure. fit the ae finder and the camera gains aperture-priority automatic exposure. there are also waist-level and high-magnification finders, suited to macro, copying and specialist work. motor drives and automatic exposure: with the ae power winder or ae motor drive fitted, the camera offers shutter-priority automatic exposure as well as continuous shooting. in other words, depending on the accessories fitted, the same new f-1 can be a manual camera, an aperture-priority camera or a shutter-priority camera. interchangeable focusing screens: the new f-1 offers a range of focusing screens. more unusually, changing the screen also changes the metering pattern, so photographers could choose average, partial or spot metering to suit the subject. linking the metering mode to the focusing screen in this way was unique among cameras of its time. built for professional use the new f-1 has a metal body and a robust construction that stands up to the demands of news, sports and outdoor photography. canon put particular emphasis on reliability, and the body was rigorously tested to work dependably in extreme temperatures and under heavy use. the camera soon became the main tool of many professionals and was a familiar sight at news events and major sporting competitions. canon also produced a los angeles olympics commemorative edition, underlining its standing in sports photography. the fd lens system the new f-1 uses the canon fd mount and gives access to the large range of fd lenses, from ultra-wides and standards to super-telephotos. the l-series lenses use fluorite and special low-dispersion elements for outstanding image quality, and they were essential tools for news and sports photographers. with such a complete system of lenses and accessories, the new f-1 could handle almost any assignment. the final chapter of the fd era in 1987 canon introduced the eos autofocus system with the new ef mount, and the fd system was gradually replaced. the new f-1 stayed in production into the early 1990s as the last professional flagship of the fd system. canon's later flagships, such as the eos-1, belonged fully to the autofocus age. the new f-1 is still sought after by many film enthusiasts and collectors on the second-hand market. its tough body, flexible configuration and the reassurance of its mechanical shutter have made it shine again as film photography makes a comeback. conclusion the new f-1 was born at the turning point between two eras. it embraced the convenience of electronics without giving up the reliability of a mechanical camera, and its modular design met the needs of very different photographers, showing how well canon understood the professional market. as the last fd flagship, the new f-1 is more than a camera. it sums up canon's manual-focus era.  canon 佳能 new f-1 新f-1 單鏡反光機 菲林相機 fd卡口 專業旗艦 混合式快門 模組化系統 新聞攝影 體育攝影 相機歷史 canon f-1 slr film camera fd mount professional flagship hybrid shutter modular system interchangeable finder 四大專業旗艦比較：nikon f、canon new f-1、minolta x-1、pentax lx  four professional flagships compared: nikon f, canon new f-1, minolta x-1 and pentax lx      四大專業旗艦比較：nikon f、canon new f-1、minolta x-1、pentax lx 1960至80年代，是35mm 單鏡反光機的黃金時代。各大日本廠商紛紛推出專業旗艦，爭奪新聞、體育和專業攝影市場。nikon f、canon new f-1、minolta x-1 和 pentax lx，分別代表了四家廠商對「專業相機」的不同理解。它們不屬於同一年代，但放在一起比較，正好看到專業單反由全機械走向電子化的演變。 一、nikon f：專業單反的原點（1959） nikon f 是現代專業單反的奠基者。它採用全機械結構，不需要電池也能拍攝，配合可換觀景器、可換對焦屏、接近100%視野率的觀景器和電動捲片馬達，建立了一套完整的專業系統。 最初的眼平觀景器沒有測光功能，其後推出的 photomic 系列觀景器才加入測光。nikon f 堅固耐用，在越戰等新聞現場經受了考驗，奠定了 nikon 在專業市場的領導地位。後來的專業旗艦，幾乎都以 nikon f 為比較對象。 二、minolta x-1：電子旗艦的先行者（1973） minolta x-1 在北美稱為 xk，在歐洲稱為 xm，是 minolta 第一部真正的專業旗艦。它比其他對手更早擁抱電子化，以電子快門提供光圈優先自動曝光，在當年相當前衛。 x-1 同樣採用模組化設計，有可換觀景器和對焦屏，亦可配上馬達。不過，它的電子設計依賴電池，在專業攝影師眼中可靠性不及機械相機，加上 minolta 在專業市場的服務網絡不及 nikon 和 canon，x-1 的銷量有限，今天反而成為收藏家眼中較罕見的機型。 三、pentax lx：精巧耐用的長壽旗艦（1980） pentax lx 在1980年推出，是 pentax 的專業旗艦，亦是四部之中體積最小巧的一部。 lx 最大的技術特色是「片面測光」：測光元件直接讀取菲林表面反射的光線，並在曝光期間即時調整。這令它在長時間曝光時仍然能夠準確自動控制，對夜景和天文攝影尤其有用。lx 亦採用混合式快門，高速檔在沒有電池時仍能使用。機身設有防塵防水密封，在同期相機中十分少見。 lx 的生產期長達約二十年，是同類旗艦中最長壽的機型之一。 四、canon new f-1：模組化的集大成者（1981） new f-1 比 lx 晚一年面世，同樣採用混合式快門，高速檔由機械控制，電池耗盡仍可拍攝。它的特色在於高度模組化：換上 ae 觀景器就有光圈優先，裝上 ae 馬達則有快門優先；更換對焦屏亦會同時改變測光方式。一部機身可以按需要配置成不同的工具，靈活性在四部之中最高。 五、規格比較 | | nikon f | minolta x-1 | pentax lx | canon new f-1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | 推出年份 | 1959 | 1973 | 1980 | 1981 | | 卡口 | nikon f | minolta sr | pentax k | canon fd | | 快門控制 | 全機械 | 電子 | 混合式 | 混合式 | | 無電池拍攝 | 可以 | 有限 | 高速檔可用 | 高速檔可用 | | 自動曝光 | 沒有 | 光圈優先 | 光圈優先 | 光圈及快門優先（視配件） | | 可換觀景器 | 有 | 有 | 有 | 有 | | 主要特色 | 開創專業系統 | 電子化先鋒 | 片面測光、防塵防水 | 高度模組化 | 六、四種設計哲學 把四部相機放在一起看，可以見到四種不同取向： nikon f 代表可靠：全機械結構，簡單、耐用、不依賴電池，是專業工具的原型。 minolta x-1 代表前瞻：最早押注電子化，技術領先，卻未能在保守的專業市場建立信心。 pentax lx 代表精巧：在細小的機身內加入先進測光和密封設計，以技術取勝而非體積。 canon new f-1 代表靈活：以模組化回應不同需要，把電子便利和機械可靠結合起來。 有趣的是，lx 和 new f-1 都選擇了混合式快門。這說明到了八十年代初，業界已經得出共識：專業相機需要電子化帶來的便利，但不能完全放棄機械的保障。minolta x-1 走得太早，nikon f 則屬於上一個時代，兩者正好位於這條演變路線的兩端。 七、結語 這四部相機各有所長，沒有絕對的高下之分。nikon f 建立了規則，minolta x-1 嘗試改寫規則，pentax lx 和 canon new f-1 則在規則之內追求極致。今天在二手市場，它們都是菲林愛好者和收藏家的心頭好。選擇哪一部，取決於你更重視機械的可靠、電子的便利、機身的精巧，還是系統的靈活。  four professional flagships compared: nikon f, canon new f-1, minolta x-1 and pentax lx the 1960s to the 1980s were the golden age of the 35mm slr. japan's major manufacturers all launched professional flagships to compete for the news, sports and professional markets. the nikon f, canon new f-1, minolta x-1 and pentax lx each show how one maker understood the idea of a "professional camera". they don't all come from the same era, but comparing them shows how the professional slr evolved from fully mechanical to electronic. nikon f: where the professional slr began (1959) the nikon f laid the foundations of the modern professional slr. it is fully mechanical and works without a battery. interchangeable finders and focusing screens, a viewfinder with close to 100% coverage and a motor drive gave it a complete professional system. the original eye-level finder had no meter; metering arrived later with the photomic series of finders. the nikon f was extremely tough, proved itself in news coverage such as the vietnam war, and established nikon's leadership in the professional market. almost every professional flagship that followed was measured against it. minolta x-1: an early electronic flagship (1973) the minolta x-1, sold as the xk in north america and the xm in europe, was minolta's first true professional flagship. it embraced electronics earlier than its rivals, using an electronic shutter to offer aperture-priority automatic exposure, which was very advanced for its day. the x-1 was also modular, with interchangeable finders and focusing screens and an optional motor drive. however, its electronic design depended on batteries, and professionals saw it as less reliable than a mechanical camera. minolta's professional service network also lagged behind nikon's and canon's. as a result, the x-1 sold in modest numbers, and today it is a relatively rare camera that collectors seek out. pentax lx: a compact, long-lived flagship (1980) the pentax lx arrived in 1980 as pentax's professional flagship. it is the smallest of the four. its key technical feature is off-the-film metering. the meter reads light reflected from the surface of the film and adjusts the exposure in real time while the shutter is open. this lets it control long automatic exposures accurately, which is especially useful for night and astronomical photography. the lx also has a hybrid shutter, so the fast speeds still work without a battery. its body is sealed against dust and moisture, which was very unusual at the time. the lx stayed in production for about 20 years, making it one of the longest-lived professional flagships. canon new f-1: modularity perfected (1981) the new f-1 arrived a year after the lx and also uses a hybrid shutter. its fast speeds are mechanically controlled, so it can keep shooting with a dead battery. what sets it apart is its high degree of modularity. fit the ae finder and you get aperture priority. fit the ae motor drive and you get shutter priority. changing the focusing screen also changes the metering pattern. a single body can be configured into different tools as needed, making it the most flexible of the four. specifications compared | | nikon f | minolta x-1 | pentax lx | canon new f-1 | |---|---|---|---|---| | launched | 1959 | 1973 | 1980 | 1981 | | mount | nikon f | minolta sr | pentax k | canon fd | | shutter control | fully mechanical | electronic | hybrid | hybrid | | shooting without a battery | yes | limited | fast speeds | fast speeds | | automatic exposure | none | aperture priority | aperture priority | aperture and shutter priority (depending on accessories) | | interchangeable finders | yes | yes | yes | yes | | defining feature | created the professional system | electronics pioneer | off-the-film metering, weather sealing | highly modular | four design philosophies seen together, the four cameras reflect four different priorities: the nikon f stands for reliability: fully mechanical, simple, tough and independent of batteries, it is the prototype of the professional tool. the minolta x-1 stands for vision: it bet on electronics first and led on technology, but it never won the confidence of a conservative professional market. the pentax lx stands for refinement: it packs advanced metering and sealing into a small body, winning on technology rather than size. the canon new f-1 stands for flexibility: its modularity meets different needs and combines electronic convenience with mechanical reliability. interestingly, the lx and the new f-1 both chose a hybrid shutter. this shows that by the early 1980s the industry had reached a consensus. professional cameras needed the convenience of electronics, but they couldn't give up the security of mechanics altogether. the minolta x-1 came too early and the nikon f belonged to an earlier era, so the two sit at opposite ends of this line of development. conclusion each of these four cameras has its own strengths, and none is simply better than the others. the nikon f set the rules, the minolta x-1 tried to rewrite them, and the pentax lx and canon new f-1 pushed for perfection within them. all four are favourites with film enthusiasts and collectors on the second-hand market today. which one to choose depends on what you value most: mechanical reliability, electronic convenience, a compact body or a flexible system.  nikon f canon new f-1 minolta x-1 pentax lx 尼康 佳能 美能達 賓得 專業旗艦 單鏡反光機 菲林相機 混合式快門 機械相機 相機比較 相機歷史 nikon canon minolta holga：香港製造的塑膠傳奇  holga: the plastic legend made in hong kong      holga：香港製造的塑膠傳奇 在相機世界裏，大多數品牌都在追求更銳利、更準確、更完美的影像。holga 卻反其道而行：塑膠機身、塑膠鏡頭、漏光、暗角、失焦，這些在一般相機上被視為缺陷的特點，反而成為它最迷人的地方。這部價錢低廉的玩具相機，由香港出發，走進了全世界的藝術館和攝影課堂。 一、香港出生的平民相機 holga 誕生於1980年代初的香港，由李定明（t. m. lee）創辦的公司設計及生產。據常見的說法，holga 這個名字來自粵語「好光」的發音，寓意影像明亮。 holga 最初並非為藝術創作而設計。當時中國內地市場仍然以120菲林為主流，普羅大眾需要一部便宜、耐用、容易使用的相機拍攝家庭照和生活照，holga 正是為這個市場而生。它結構簡單、成本極低，任何人都可以拿起就拍。 然而，隨着35mm 菲林在內地迅速普及，holga 原本的市場很快萎縮。這部相機本來可能就此被遺忘，卻意外地在另一個地方找到了新生命。 二、簡單到極致的結構 holga 的設計可以用「極簡」來形容： 塑膠鏡頭：焦距約60mm，光學質素簡單，畫面中央尚算清晰，邊緣則明顯模糊。 固定快門：快門速度大約固定在1/100秒，另設 b 門可作長時間曝光。 光圈選擇：機身上有「晴天」和「陰天」兩個標記。不少型號兩者的實際光圈分別極小，更多是一種心理安慰。 區域對焦：以人像、小組、團體和山景四個圖示估計距離，全憑目測。 120菲林：使用中片幅菲林，附有片框，可以拍攝6×6 正方形或6×4.5 格式。 機身由塑膠製成，後蓋密封性不佳，經常出現漏光，不少用家會用黑色膠紙把接縫封好，亦有人故意保留漏光效果。 三、「缺陷」成為風格 holga 的影像有幾個鮮明特徵：強烈的暗角、柔和甚至模糊的邊緣、不可預測的漏光，以及塑膠鏡頭帶來的夢幻感。這些特徵令照片帶有一種懷舊、朦朧、帶點超現實的氣氛，是任何高級鏡頭都無法複製的。 九十年代以後，holga 在歐美攝影界和藝術學院之間流行起來。不少攝影老師用它作教學工具，讓學生擺脫對器材的依賴，專注觀察、構圖和感受。一些專業攝影師亦用 holga 創作，作品甚至登上雜誌、獲獎和進入藝廊展覽，證明好照片不一定需要昂貴的器材。 四、lomography 浪潮 holga 的流行，與 lomography 運動密不可分。lomography 提倡「不要思考，只管拍攝」，鼓勵用家隨心所欲地拍照，擁抱意外和不完美。holga 的隨機性和不可預測，正好符合這種精神，因此成為 lomography 圈子的代表相機之一。 隨着需求增加，holga 推出了多款變化型號，例如內置閃燈的120n、附彩色閃燈的120cfn，以及使用35mm 菲林的135系列、針孔相機版本、雙鏡反光版本等，讓用家有更多選擇。 五、停產與延續 踏入數碼年代，菲林需求大幅下降，holga 的原廠生產亦在2010年代中期停止。不過，holga 的影響力並未消失。它的鏡頭被改裝成數碼相機鏡頭，手機應用程式亦紛紛模仿「holga 效果」，暗角和漏光濾鏡成為社交媒體上的常見風格。近年菲林攝影復興，二手 holga 再次受到年輕一代歡迎。 六、結語 holga 是一部奇妙的相機。它的出身平凡，原意只是讓普通人拍照，卻在另一片土地上成為藝術創作工具。它提醒我們，攝影的核心不在於器材是否完美，而在於拍攝者的眼光和感受。對於香港人來說，holga 更是一段值得驕傲的故事：一部本地設計的塑膠相機，憑着它的「不完美」，在世界攝影史上留下了自己的名字。  holga: the plastic legend made in hong kong most camera brands chase sharper, more accurate, more perfect images. holga goes the other way. it has a plastic body, a plastic lens, light leaks, vignetting and soft focus. on most cameras these would count as flaws, but on the holga they are what make it so appealing. this cheap toy camera started out in hong kong and found its way into galleries and photography classrooms around the world. a people's camera born in hong kong the holga was born in hong kong in the early 1980s, designed and made by a company founded by t. m. lee. the name is commonly said to come from the cantonese phrase ho gwong (好光), meaning "very bright". the holga was not designed for art. at the time, 120 film was still the norm in mainland china, and ordinary people needed a cheap, tough, easy camera for family snaps and everyday pictures. the holga was made for that market. its construction was simple and its cost was very low, so anyone could pick it up and start shooting. as 35mm film spread rapidly across mainland china, though, the holga's original market soon shrank. the camera might have been forgotten, but it found an unexpected new life somewhere else. simplicity taken to the extreme the holga's design can fairly be called minimalist: plastic lens: the focal length is about 60mm. the optics are basic, reasonably sharp in the centre and clearly soft at the edges. fixed shutter: the shutter speed is fixed at roughly 1/100 sec, and a b setting allows long exposures. aperture settings: the body is marked "sunny" and "cloudy". on many models the actual difference between the two is tiny, so they are more reassurance than real control. zone focusing: four symbols stand for distances: a single portrait, a small group, a large group and mountains. it is all down to guesswork. 120 film: it takes medium-format film and comes with masks for 6×6 square or 6×4.5 frames. the body is plastic and the back does not seal well, so light leaks are common. many users tape the seams with black tape, while others keep the leaks on purpose. flaws become a style holga pictures have a few distinctive traits. there is heavy vignetting, soft or even blurry edges, unpredictable light leaks and a dreamy quality from the plastic lens. together they give photographs a nostalgic, hazy, slightly surreal mood that no premium lens can reproduce. from the 1990s, the holga caught on among photographers and art schools in europe and north america. many photography teachers used it to wean students off their reliance on equipment so they could concentrate on seeing, composition and feeling. some professionals also made work with the holga, and their pictures appeared in magazines, won awards and were shown in galleries. they proved that a good photograph doesn't need expensive equipment. the lomography wave the holga's popularity is closely tied to the lomography movement. lomography's motto is "don't think, just shoot". it encourages people to take pictures freely and to welcome accidents and imperfection. the holga's randomness and unpredictability fit that spirit perfectly, and it became one of the movement's signature cameras. as demand grew, new versions appeared. they include the 120n with a built-in flash, the 120cfn with a colour flash, the 135 series for 35mm film, pinhole versions and a twin-lens reflex, giving users far more choice. discontinuation and legacy when the digital era arrived, demand for film fell sharply, and original holga production ended in the mid-2010s. its influence did not disappear, though. holga lenses have been adapted for digital cameras, phone apps imitate the "holga effect", and vignetting and light-leak filters are a familiar style on social media. with the recent film revival, second-hand holgas are popular again with a younger generation. conclusion the holga is a remarkable camera. it came from humble beginnings, intended only to let ordinary people take pictures, and yet it became an artistic tool in another part of the world. it reminds us that photography is not about perfect equipment but about the photographer's eye and feeling. for people from hong kong, it is also a story to be proud of: a locally designed plastic camera whose "imperfections" earned it a place in the history of photography.  holga toy camera plastic camera hong kong 120 film medium format lomography light leaks vignetting 蔡司經典光學設計：鏡頭名字背後的光學密碼  classic zeiss optical designs: the code behind the lens names      蔡司經典光學設計：鏡頭名字背後的光學密碼 拿起一支蔡司鏡頭，鏡筒上總會刻着一個名字：planar、sonnar、distagon……這些名字並非隨意的產品型號，而是代表不同的光學結構。每個名字背後，都有一段光學設計史。認識這些設計，就能明白為甚麼不同的蔡司鏡頭，會拍出截然不同的影像性格。 一、protar：消像散的起點 蔡司在十九世紀末已經是顯微鏡光學的權威，後來由科學家 paul rudolph 帶領，進軍攝影鏡頭領域。1890年，rudolph 設計的 protar 面世，是最早期的消像散（anastigmat）鏡頭之一，能夠同時改善畫面中央和邊緣的清晰度。protar 本身今天已很少人提及，但它奠定了蔡司攝影光學的基礎，此後多款經典設計都由此發展而來。 二、planar：對稱結構的典範 1896年，rudolph 設計了 planar。它以雙高斯（double gauss）結構為基礎，前後兩組鏡片大致對稱，能有效抑制像差，令成像平坦均勻，planar 這個名字正源自「平面」的意思。 不過，planar 的鏡片空氣接觸面多，在沒有鍍膜的年代容易產生眩光，因此早期未能普及。直到鍍膜技術成熟，planar 才真正發揮潛力，成為今天大光圈標準鏡頭最常見的結構。contax 的 planar 50mm f/1.4 和 85mm f/1.4，以及哈蘇相機上的 planar 80mm f/2.8，都是攝影史上的名鏡。 最傳奇的 planar，是光圈達 f/0.7 的 50mm 鏡頭。它原本為太空計劃製造，後來被導演 stanley kubrick 用來在燭光下拍攝電影《barry lyndon》，成為影史佳話。 三、tessar：簡潔的「鷹眼」 1902年，rudolph 再推出 tessar，只用三組四片鏡片，結構簡單，卻有出色的銳利度和反差，因而有「鷹眼」（adlerauge）的美譽。 tessar 的優點是體積小、成本低、易於生產，因此成為二十世紀產量最大的鏡頭設計之一，由摺疊相機、旁軸相機以至餅乾鏡頭，都可以見到它的身影。蔡司的 tessar 專利亦被多家廠商參考，影響遍及整個相機工業。 四、sonnar：大光圈的先鋒 sonnar 由光學設計師 ludwig bertele 在1930年前後設計。它的特點是把多片鏡片膠合在一起，減少空氣接觸面，在當時鍍膜技術未成熟的情況下，有效減少眩光，並提供當年罕見的大光圈。 sonnar 隨蔡司伊康的 contax 旁軸相機成名，其中 50mm f/1.5 更是當時最快的標準鏡頭之一。sonnar 的影像反差高、焦外柔和，後來發展成中長焦鏡頭的主要結構，例如 contax 的 sonnar 135mm f/2.8 和哈蘇的 sonnar 150mm f/4。 五、biogon：旁軸廣角的巔峰 biogon 同樣出自 bertele 之手。戰後的 biogon 採用近乎對稱的超廣角結構，後組鏡片非常貼近菲林，因此變形極低、邊緣畫質出色。 不過，這種結構需要鏡頭後端深入機身，只適合沒有反光鏡的旁軸相機。哈蘇 swc 超廣角相機上的 biogon 38mm f/4.5，就是最經典的例子，至今仍被視為變形控制最好的廣角鏡頭之一。 六、distagon：為單反而生的廣角 單鏡反光機的反光鏡需要活動空間，鏡頭後端不能太貼近菲林，biogon 式的設計因此無法使用。蔡司的答案是 distagon：採用反望遠（retrofocus）結構，前面加入大型負透鏡組，讓後焦距延長，騰出反光鏡的活動空間。 distagon 成為蔡司單反廣角鏡頭的標準設計，contax 的 distagon 35mm f/1.4、28mm f/2，以及哈蘇的 distagon 50mm，都是廣受讚譽的作品。 七、hologon：極簡的超廣角實驗 hologon 是一個特別的設計，只用極少量的鏡片達成超廣角視角，光圈固定而細小，但變形控制極佳。它產量不多，屬於收藏級的光學實驗品，展現了蔡司在光學設計上的大膽創新。 八、結語 由 protar 到 hologon，每一個蔡司鏡頭名字，都代表一種解決光學問題的思路：planar 追求平坦，tessar 追求簡潔，sonnar 突破光圈，biogon 和 distagon 則分別為旁軸和單反解決廣角難題。了解這些設計，下次拿起蔡司鏡頭時，你看到的不只是一個名字，而是一百多年的光學智慧。  classic zeiss optical designs: the code behind the lens names pick up a zeiss lens and you will always find a name engraved on the barrel: planar, sonnar, distagon and so on. these are not arbitrary model numbers. each one stands for a particular optical formula with its own history. once you understand these designs, you can see why different zeiss lenses produce images with such different characters. protar: where the anastigmat began by the late nineteenth century, zeiss was already the authority on microscope optics. led by the scientist paul rudolph, it then moved into photographic lenses. rudolph's protar appeared in 1890. it was one of the earliest anastigmats, lenses that improved sharpness in the centre and at the edges at the same time. few people mention the protar today, but it laid the foundations of zeiss photographic optics, and several classic designs grew out of it. planar: the model of symmetry in 1896 rudolph designed the planar. it is based on the double gauss formula. the front and rear groups are broadly symmetrical, which keeps aberrations well under control and gives a flat, even image. that is where the name comes from. the planar has many glass-to-air surfaces, though, and before lens coatings existed it was prone to flare, so it did not catch on at first. only once coating technology matured did the planar reach its potential. it is now the most common formula for fast standard lenses. the contax planar 50mm f/1.4 and 85mm f/1.4, and the hasselblad planar 80mm f/2.8, are among the great lenses of photographic history. the most legendary planar is a 50mm with an aperture of f/0.7. it was originally made for the space programme and was later used by the director stanley kubrick to shoot scenes lit only by candlelight in barry lyndon, which has become a famous story in film history. tessar: the simple "eagle eye" in 1902 rudolph introduced the tessar. with just four elements in three groups it is simple, yet it delivers excellent sharpness and contrast, and it earned the nickname "eagle eye" (adlerauge). the tessar is compact, cheap and easy to make. that made it one of the most widely produced lens designs of the twentieth century, found in everything from folding cameras and rangefinders to pancake lenses. many manufacturers drew on the tessar patent, and its influence spread through the whole camera industry. sonnar: a pioneer of fast apertures the optical designer ludwig bertele created the sonnar around 1930. its defining feature is cementing several elements together to reduce the number of glass-to-air surfaces. before coatings matured, this cut flare effectively and made possible apertures that were rare at the time. the sonnar made its name on zeiss ikon's contax rangefinders, and the 50mm f/1.5 was among the fastest standard lenses of its day. sonnars give high contrast with soft out-of-focus areas, and the formula later became the main design for short and medium telephotos, such as the contax sonnar 135mm f/2.8 and the hasselblad sonnar 150mm f/4. biogon: the height of rangefinder wide-angles the biogon was also bertele's work. the post-war biogon uses an almost symmetrical ultra-wide formula, with the rear elements sitting very close to the film. this gives extremely low distortion and excellent edge quality. the design needs the back of the lens to reach deep into the body, though, so it only suits rangefinder cameras without a mirror. the classic example is the biogon 38mm f/4.5 on the hasselblad swc, which is still regarded as one of the best wide-angle lenses ever made for controlling distortion. distagon: a wide-angle built for the slr an slr's mirror needs room to move, so the back of the lens can't sit too close to the film, and a biogon-style design won't fit. zeiss's answer was the distagon. it uses a retrofocus formula: a large negative group at the front extends the back focus and leaves space for the mirror. the distagon became zeiss's standard design for slr wide-angles. the contax distagon 35mm f/1.4 and 28mm f/2, and the hasselblad distagon 50mm, are all highly regarded. hologon: a minimalist ultra-wide experiment the hologon is an unusual design. it achieves an ultra-wide angle of view with very few elements. its aperture is small and fixed, but distortion is superbly controlled. few were made, and it is now a collector's piece, an optical experiment that shows how bold zeiss could be. conclusion from protar to hologon, each zeiss lens name stands for a way of solving an optical problem. the planar aims for flatness and the tessar for simplicity. the sonnar pushed apertures wider, while the biogon and distagon solved the wide-angle problem for rangefinders and slrs respectively. once you know these designs, a zeiss lens is more than a name. it carries more than a century of optical thinking.  蔡司 carl zeiss 光學設計 鏡頭結構 planar tessar sonnar biogon distagon protar hologon 雙高斯 反望遠 鏡頭歷史 zeiss optical design lens design double gauss retrofocus lens history  鏡頭  contax rts iii：手動對焦年代的旗艦終章  contax rts iii: the last word in manual-focus flagships      contax rts iii：手動對焦年代的旗艦終章 如果說 contax rts 開創了德日合作的傳奇，那麼 rts iii 就是這條路線的巔峰之作。它在1990年面世，當時自動對焦相機已經席捲市場，京瓷旗下的 contax 卻選擇推出一部堅守手動對焦的旗艦單鏡反光機，把傳統專業機身的每一個環節都做到極致。 一、逆流而上的定位 八十年代中期以後，各大廠商紛紛轉向自動對焦，專業旗艦亦不例外。contax 的策略卻截然不同：蔡司 c/y 鏡頭群是手動對焦設計，品牌的核心價值在於光學質素，而不是對焦速度。rts iii 因此把精力放在影像質素、測光精度和機身可靠性上，目標用家是追求極致畫質的專業攝影師和高階愛好者。 二、陶瓷真空吸片板：從菲林平面着手 rts iii 最著名的創新，是陶瓷真空吸片板，contax 稱之為 rtv（real time vacuum）系統。 菲林本身並非完全平整，尤其在溫度和濕度變化下，片面會輕微彎曲。對一般鏡頭來說影響不大，但對於解像力極高的蔡司鏡頭，特別是在大光圈拍攝時，菲林平面稍有偏差，焦點便會偏移。rts iii 在後蓋的壓片板上加入細小氣孔，並以陶瓷製造壓片板，拍攝時把菲林吸貼在平整的陶瓷表面上，確保整格菲林保持在同一平面，讓蔡司鏡頭的解像力得到充分發揮。 這種從菲林平面入手提升畫質的做法，在35mm 單鏡反光機之中十分罕見，亦最能體現 contax 對影像質素的執着。 三、專業級的機身規格 rts iii 在規格上毫不妥協： 高速快門：電子控制焦平面快門，最高速度達 1/8000 秒，閃燈同步速度達 1/250 秒，在當年屬頂尖水平。 全視野觀景器：觀景器視野率接近100%，所見即所得，方便精確構圖。 多種測光模式：提供中央重點測光和點測光等模式，配合曝光補償和包圍曝光，讓攝影師精準控制曝光。 內置馬達：機身內置捲片馬達，無需另購配件便能連續拍攝。 反光鏡預升：有助減少慢速快門下的機震，對微距和風景拍攝尤其重要。 四、延續「實時」理念 rts iii 保留了 rts 系列的核心精神：輕觸即發的電磁快門釋放鈕。按下快門至實際曝光的延遲極短，攝影師可以準確捕捉瞬間。這種手感由第一代 rts 延續至 rts iii，成為整個系列最具辨識度的特色。 機身設計亦承接了前代的簡潔風格，控制轉盤清晰易用，但整體更加堅固耐用，重量和體積都反映出它作為專業工具的定位。 五、與蔡司鏡頭的完美配搭 rts iii 採用 c/y 卡口，可以使用全系列蔡司 t 鏡頭。由超廣角 distagon、標準 planar，以至長焦 sonnar，加上多支微距和特殊用途鏡頭，構成了一個完整的專業系統。真空吸片板讓這些鏡頭的光學潛力得到完全發揮，機身與鏡頭之間的配合，正是 rts iii 最大的價值所在。 六、時代的句號 rts iii 生產了十多年，一直是 contax 手動對焦系統的旗艦。其後 contax 推出了自動對焦的 n 系列，但 c/y 系統的用家始終對 rts iii 情有獨鍾。隨着京瓷在2005年退出相機業務，rts iii 亦成為 contax 手動對焦旗艦的最後一章。 今天，rts iii 在二手市場仍然備受追捧。不少用家認為，它代表了35mm 手動對焦單鏡反光機所能達到的最高水平。 七、結語 rts iii 是一部不追隨潮流的相機。在自動對焦成為主流的年代，它選擇回到攝影最根本的問題：怎樣讓影像更清晰、更準確。陶瓷真空吸片板、1/8000 秒快門、全視野觀景器，每一項設計都為畫質服務。對於欣賞蔡司鏡頭的攝影人來說，rts iii 不只是一部相機，更是發揮蔡司光學的最佳舞台。  contax rts iii: the last word in manual-focus flagships if the contax rts started the german–japanese legend, the rts iii was its high point. it appeared in 1990, when autofocus cameras had already taken over the market. contax, by then part of kyocera, chose to launch a flagship slr that stayed with manual focus, and it refined every part of the traditional professional body as far as it could go. going against the tide from the mid-1980s onwards, the major manufacturers moved to autofocus, including for their professional flagships. contax took a very different path. the zeiss c/y lenses were manual-focus designs, and the brand's core value lay in optical quality rather than focusing speed. so the rts iii concentrated on image quality, metering accuracy and reliability. it was aimed at professionals and serious enthusiasts who wanted the best possible image quality. the ceramic vacuum pressure plate: starting with the film plane the rts iii's best-known innovation is its ceramic vacuum pressure plate, which contax called the rtv (real time vacuum) system. film is never perfectly flat, and it curls slightly as temperature and humidity change. with ordinary lenses this hardly matters. with high-resolution zeiss lenses, especially when shooting wide open, even a small departure from the film plane can shift the point of focus. the rts iii's ceramic pressure plate has tiny holes in it. when you take a picture, suction holds the film against its flat ceramic surface, so the whole frame stays in one plane and the zeiss lenses can resolve all the detail they are capable of. improving image quality by starting with the film plane was very unusual in a 35mm slr, and nothing shows contax's devotion to image quality more clearly. professional specifications the rts iii made no compromises on specification: fast shutter: an electronically controlled focal-plane shutter with a top speed of 1/8000 sec and flash sync at 1/250 sec, which was top-tier at the time. full-coverage viewfinder: close to 100% coverage, so what you see is what you get, which helps with precise framing. multiple metering modes: including centre-weighted and spot, with exposure compensation and auto bracketing for precise control of exposure. built-in motor: the film winder is built in, so you can shoot continuously without buying an accessory. mirror lock-up: this reduces vibration at slow shutter speeds, which matters most in macro and landscape work. carrying on the "real time" idea the rts iii kept the core idea of the rts series: an electromagnetic shutter release that fires at the lightest touch. the delay between pressing the button and the actual exposure is extremely short, so photographers can capture the moment precisely. this feel ran from the first rts through to the rts iii and became the most recognisable trait of the whole series. the body keeps the clean style of its predecessors, with clear and easy-to-use dials. it is sturdier overall, though, and its weight and size reflect its role as a professional tool. a perfect match for zeiss lenses the rts iii uses the c/y mount and accepts the full range of zeiss t lenses. from ultra-wide distagons and standard planars to telephoto sonnars, plus several macro and special-purpose lenses, they form a complete professional system. the vacuum pressure plate lets these lenses reach their full optical potential. that partnership between body and lens is the rts iii's greatest strength. the end of an era the rts iii stayed in production for more than a decade as the flagship of contax's manual-focus system. contax later launched the autofocus n series, but c/y users stayed loyal to the rts iii. when kyocera left the camera business in 2005, the rts iii became the final chapter of contax's manual-focus that refused to follow fashion. when autofocus became the norm, it went back to photography's most basic question: how to make images sharper and more accurate. the ceramic vacuum pressure plate, the 1/8000 sec shutter and the full-coverage viewfinder all serve image quality. for photographers who appreciate zeiss lenses, the rts iii is more than a camera. it is the best stage there is for zeiss optics.  contax contax rts iii kyocera carl zeiss zeiss t* ceramic vacuum pressure plate rtv slr film camera c/y mount manual focus camera history  相機機身  camera bodies  no.004

contax rts：德日合璧的傳奇單鏡反光機  contax rts: the legendary slr that united germany and japan      contax rts：德日合璧的傳奇單鏡反光機 在單鏡反光機的歷史上，contax rts 是一部很特別的相機：德國光學、日本製造、保時捷設計，三者合一。它在1970年代中期面世，為 contax 這個名字開啟了往後三十年的新篇章。 一、contax 名字的復活 contax 原是蔡司伊康（zeiss ikon）在1930年代推出的旁軸相機品牌，曾與徠卡分庭抗禮。戰後蔡司伊康相機業務不斷萎縮，在七十年代初全面退出相機生產，contax 這個名字也隨之沉寂。 蔡司雖然退出了相機製造，仍然希望自己的鏡頭有一個高端的機身平台。當時日本的雅西卡（yashica）需要一個有分量的品牌來提升形象，雙方一拍即合。蔡司把 contax 品牌授權給雅西卡，由雅西卡負責機身，蔡司負責鏡頭設計，兩家合作的第一部產品就是 contax rts。 二、保時捷設計的外形 rts 的外形設計由保時捷設計團隊參與。機身線條簡潔俐落，稜角分明而不失圓潤，控制轉盤排列清晰，握持感舒適。在當年一片以功能堆砌為主的日本單鏡反光機之中，rts 的外觀顯得格外現代，即使以今天的眼光來看，仍然不覺過時。 三、「實時系統」的意義 rts 是「real time system」的縮寫，意思是「實時系統」。它最大的賣點，是採用電磁快門釋放鈕。傳統機械快門鈕要按下一段相當長的行程，才能觸發快門；rts 的快門鈕行程極短，輕輕一觸便能釋放快門，大大縮短了按下快門至實際曝光之間的延遲。對於拍攝動態題材、講求捕捉決定性瞬間的攝影師來說，這是實實在在的優勢。 這個「實時」的理念亦貫穿整個系統，包括可以接駁電動捲片器及馬達，讓相機的反應和連拍能力配合專業需要。 四、電子化的機身 rts 屬於七十年代中期新一代的電子單鏡反光機，快門由電子控制，提供光圈優先自動曝光和全手動模式，觀景器內以指示燈顯示快門速度，方便攝影師一邊構圖一邊掌握曝光。機身需要電池驅動，這在當年仍屬較新的設計取向，亦反映了雅西卡在電子相機方面的技術積累。 五、蔡司 t 鏡頭群 用家選擇 contax，很大程度是為了蔡司鏡頭。rts 採用 contax/yashica 卡口，通常簡稱為 c/y 卡口，配合一系列蔡司 t 多層鍍膜鏡頭，包括 planar、distagon、sonnar 等經典設計。其中 planar 50mm f/1.4 和 planar 85mm f/1.4 最受歡迎，以豐富的色彩、立體感和細膩的焦外表現見稱，被不少人稱為「蔡司味道」。 這些鏡頭部分在德國生產，後期則轉由日本工廠製造，但光學設計仍由蔡司把關。c/y 鏡頭今天在二手市場依然十分搶手，不少人把它們轉接到無反機身上使用，繼續發揮餘熱。 六、rts 家族的延續 rts 取得成功後，contax 陸續推出後繼機型。rts ii 在八十年代初面世，改用石英控制快門，精度更高；rts iii 則在九十年代推出，加入陶瓷真空吸片板等創新設計，確保菲林平整，把 rts 系列推向頂峰。雅西卡其後被京瓷（kyocera）收購，contax 系列在京瓷旗下繼續發展，直至京瓷在2005年退出相機業務，contax 品牌才正式畫上句號。 七、結語 contax rts 的意義，不止在於它是一部優秀的相機，更在於它證明了德國光學與日本製造可以完美結合。蔡司的鏡頭、雅西卡的機身工藝，再加上保時捷的設計美學，造就了一個橫跨三十年的系統。今天拿起一部 rts，仍然能感受到那份輕觸即發的快門手感，以及蔡司鏡頭帶來的獨特影像。這正是它令人念念不忘的原因。  contax rts: the legendary slr that united germany and japan the contax rts holds a special place in the history of the single-lens reflex. german optics, japanese manufacturing and porsche design came together in one camera. it appeared in the mid-1970s and began a new chapter for the contax name that lasted three decades. the revival of the contax name contax began in the 1930s as a zeiss ikon rangefinder brand and was once a serious rival to leica. after the war, zeiss ikon's camera business shrank steadily. in the early 1970s it stopped making cameras altogether, and the contax name fell silent. although zeiss had left camera manufacturing, it still wanted a high-end body for its lenses. at the same time, yashica in japan needed a prestigious brand to lift its image. the fit was obvious. zeiss licensed the contax name to yashica. yashica would build the bodies and zeiss would design the lenses. the first product of that partnership was the contax rts. a body shaped by porsche design the porsche design team took part in shaping the rts. the body has clean, crisp lines that are angular without being harsh, the control dials are logically arranged, and it sits comfortably in the hand. most japanese slrs of the day piled on features with little thought for form, so the rts looked strikingly modern beside them. even by today's standards it doesn't look dated. what "real time system" meant rts stands for "real time system". the camera's headline feature was its electromagnetic shutter release. a conventional mechanical release has to travel a fair distance before it fires the shutter. the rts release has a very short travel, and the lightest touch trips it. this greatly reduces the delay between pressing the button and the moment of exposure. for photographers shooting moving subjects and chasing the decisive moment, that was a genuine advantage. the same "real time" idea ran through the whole system. the camera could take a power winder and a motor drive, so its responsiveness and shooting speed could keep up with professional needs. an electronic body the rts belonged to the new generation of electronic slrs that arrived in the mid-1970s. its shutter was electronically controlled. it offered aperture-priority automatic exposure and full manual mode, and indicator lights in the viewfinder showed the shutter speed. this let photographers keep track of exposure while composing. the body relied on a battery, which was still a relatively new approach at the time and reflected yashica's experience with electronic cameras. the zeiss t lens range for many buyers, the zeiss lenses were the main reason to choose contax. the rts uses the contax/yashica mount, usually shortened to c/y. it was served by a range of zeiss lenses with t multicoating, including classic planar, distagon and sonnar designs. the planar 50mm f/1.4 and planar 85mm f/1.4 are the best loved. they are known for rich colour, a strong sense of depth and smooth out-of-focus rendering, which many people call the "zeiss look". some of these lenses were made in germany, and production later moved to japan, but zeiss kept control of the optical design. c/y lenses are still in high demand on the second-hand market, and many photographers adapt them to mirrorless bodies to give them a second life. the rts family after the success of the rts, contax brought out successors. the rts ii arrived in the early 1980s with a quartz-controlled shutter for greater accuracy. the rts iii followed in the 1990s. its innovations included a ceramic vacuum pressure plate that kept the film perfectly flat, and it took the rts line to its peak. kyocera later acquired yashica, and the contax range continued under kyocera until the company left the camera business in 2005, which brought the contax name to a close. conclusion the contax rts matters for more than being an excellent camera. it proved that german optics and japanese manufacturing could be combined successfully. zeiss lenses, yashica's build quality and porsche's design sense together created a system that lasted thirty years. pick up an rts today and you can still feel that hair-trigger shutter release and see the distinctive images the zeiss lenses produce. that is why the camera is so fondly remembered.  contax 新福倫達：老牌子的第二人生  new voigtländer: a second life for an old name      新福倫達：老牌子的第二人生 在相機世界裏，歷史比福倫達（voigtländer）更悠久的品牌不多。今天攝影人口中的「新福倫達」，其實是一個德國老品牌和一家日本長野光學廠的故事。 一、源自維也納的光學世家 福倫達由 johann christoph voigtländer 於1756年在維也納創立，最初製造光學及測量儀器。1840年，福倫達把數學家 joseph petzval 設計的人像鏡頭投入生產。這支鏡頭的光圈約為 f/3.6，比當時常用的鏡頭快得多，把銀版攝影的曝光時間由以分鐘計縮短到以秒計，人像攝影從此變得可行。後來廠房遷往德國布倫瑞克，二十世紀推出 bessa、vito、prominent 等相機，是德國相機工業的重要一員。 戰後日本相機崛起，德國廠商經營日益困難。福倫達先歸入蔡司集團，七十年代初品牌轉到祿來（rollei）手上，之後商標幾經易手。這個二百多年的名字，一度只剩下一個空殼。 二、cosina 接手：1999年的轉捩點 1999年，日本長野縣中野市的 cosina（コシナ）取得福倫達品牌的使用權。cosina 創立於1959年，長年為其他品牌代工，不少人用過的入門單鏡反光機，其實都出自 cosina 的生產線。社長小林博文是一位狂熱的相機愛好者，他看準了一個當時沒人理會的市場：在自動對焦大行其道的年代，仍然有人想要手動、機械、精緻的相機和鏡頭。 「新福倫達」由此誕生。cosina 沒有簡單地把舊品牌貼上新產品，而是借用福倫達歷史上的名字，重新定義一條產品線。 三、bessa 系列：平價旁軸的復興 新福倫達的第一代產品是 bessa-l 旁軸相機，配 l39 螺口，同時推出 15mm f/4.5 super wide-heliar 超廣角鏡頭。在那個年代，15mm 旁軸鏡頭既罕見又昂貴，這支小巧而價格親民的超廣角一推出便引起轟動。 其後推出的 bessa-r 加入了測距聯動，r2、r3、r4 系列則改用 m 卡口，並提供不同的觀景器倍率，照顧由廣角到中焦的不同需要。對於買不起徠卡、又想體驗旁軸攝影的人來說，bessa 是最實際的入門選擇。cosina 其後亦為蔡司生產 zeiss ikon 旁軸相機及 zm 鏡頭，足見其製造水平。bessa 系列約在2015年停產，今天在二手市場仍有一批忠實用家。 四、鏡頭命名：延續歷史的密碼 新福倫達最為人津津樂道的，是它的鏡頭。cosina 沿用福倫達歷史上的鏡頭名稱，並大致按光圈劃分： nokton：大光圈系列，一般為 f/1.5 或更快，例如 35mm f/1.2、50mm f/1.1，甚至 50mm f/1.0。 ultron：中等光圈，多為 f/1.7 至 f/2。 color-skopar：輕巧的小光圈鏡頭，以體積細小見稱。 heliar：多用於超廣角及特別設計。 apo-lanthar：高規格複消色差設計，是近年品牌的旗艦系列，例如 50mm f/2 apo-lanthar 以極高解像力贏得好評。 這些鏡頭大多採用全金屬鏡身和手動對焦，對焦環阻尼順滑，光圈環手感清脆，做工在同價位中難逢對手。 五、無反年代的新舞台 數碼無反興起，反而為新福倫達打開了更大的市場。短法蘭距讓旁軸鏡頭可以經轉接環使用，cosina 亦順勢為 sony e、nikon z、fujifilm x 及 m4/3 等卡口推出原生鏡頭。其中不少加入了電子觸點，能夠傳送 exif 資料、配合機身防震及對焦放大，保留手動對焦樂趣之餘，也兼顧了現代工作流程。m4/3 的 f/0.95 nokton 系列，更成為不少影片拍攝者的心頭好。 六、結語 新福倫達的成功，在於它清楚知道自己的位置：不與大廠比拼自動對焦和速度，而是專注手動對焦、機械質感和光學個性。它讓一個幾乎消失的德國老牌子重獲新生，也讓一代攝影人以合理的價錢，享受到慢慢對焦、細心構圖的樂趣。二百多年後，福倫達這個名字仍然在鏡頭上閃亮，這本身就是一段值得記錄的傳奇。  new voigtländer: a second life for an old name few camera brands have a longer history than voigtländer. the brand photographers now call "new voigtländer" is the story of an old german name and a japanese optical factory in nagano. a viennese optical dynasty johann christoph voigtländer founded the company in vienna in 1756, first making optical and surveying instruments. in 1840, voigtländer began producing a portrait lens designed by the mathematician joseph petzval. with a maximum aperture of around f/3.6, it was far faster than the lenses of its day. it cut daguerreotype exposure times from minutes to seconds, and that made portrait photography practical. the firm later moved to braunschweig in germany, and in the twentieth century it made cameras such as the bessa, vito and prominent, becoming an important part of the german camera industry. after the war, the rise of japanese cameras made life increasingly hard for german makers. voigtländer first came under the zeiss group, and in the early 1970s the brand passed to rollei. the trademark then changed hands several times, and a name with two centuries of history was reduced to an empty shell. cosina steps in: the turning point of 1999 in 1999, cosina, based in nakano in japan's nagano prefecture, gained the right to use the voigtländer name. founded in 1959, cosina had spent decades as a contract manufacturer. many of the entry-level slrs people remember owning actually came off its production lines. its president, hirofumi kobayashi, is a passionate camera enthusiast. he spotted a market nobody else was paying attention to. even as autofocus was taking over, some photographers still wanted manual, mechanical and finely made cameras and lenses. that is how "new voigtländer" was born. cosina did not simply put an old badge on new products. it revived names from voigtländer's past to define a new product line. the bessa series: the affordable rangefinder returns new voigtländer's first product was the bessa-l, a rangefinder-style camera with an l39 screw mount. it launched alongside the 15mm f/4.5 super wide-heliar. at the time, a 15mm lens for a rangefinder was both rare and expensive, so this compact and reasonably priced ultra-wide caused a stir. the bessa-r that followed added a coupled rangefinder. the r2, r3 and r4 series moved to the m mount and offered different viewfinder magnifications for everything from wide-angle to short-telephoto work. for anyone who wanted to try rangefinder photography but couldn't afford a leica, the bessa was the most practical way in. cosina went on to make the zeiss ikon rangefinder and the zm lenses for zeiss, which shows the standard of its manufacturing. the bessa line was discontinued around 2015, but it still has a loyal following on the second-hand market. lens names: a code carried over from history voigtländer is best known today for its lenses. cosina kept the historic voigtländer lens names and broadly assigns them by aperture: nokton: the fast series, usually f/1.5 or faster. examples include the 35mm f/1.2, the 50mm f/1.1 and even a 50mm f/1.0. ultron: moderate apertures, mostly between f/1.7 and f/2. color-skopar: slower, lightweight lenses known for their small size. heliar: used mainly for ultra-wides and special designs. apo-lanthar: high-specification apochromatic designs and the brand's flagship range in recent years. the 50mm f/2 apo-lanthar, for example, has been widely praised for its exceptional resolution. most of these lenses have all-metal barrels and manual focus. the focus rings are smoothly damped and the aperture rings click crisply, and few rivals at the same price match the build quality. a new stage in the mirrorless era the rise of digital mirrorless cameras opened up an even bigger market for new voigtländer. their short flange distances let rangefinder lenses be used through adapters. cosina took the opportunity to release native lenses for sony e, nikon z, fujifilm x and micro four thirds. many of them have electronic contacts, which pass exif data to the camera and work with in-body stabilisation and focus magnification. they keep the pleasure of manual focus while fitting into a modern workflow. the f/0.95 nokton lenses for micro four thirds have also become favourites with many filmmakers. conclusion new voigtländer succeeded because it knew exactly where it stood. it never tried to beat the big makers on autofocus or speed. instead, it concentrated on manual focus, mechanical feel and optical character. it brought an all-but-vanished german name back to life, and it let a generation of photographers enjoy slow focusing and careful composition at a reasonable price. more than two and a half centuries on, the voigtländer name still appears on the front of lenses, and that alone makes it a story worth telling.  福倫達 新福倫達 voigtländer cosina 旁軸相機 bessa 手動對焦鏡頭 nokton apo-lanthar 無反鏡頭 相機品牌歷史 日本光學 new voigtländer rangefinder manual focus lenses heliar
